revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Running a Marathon
revealWordProblem.text:
Evelyn is training to run the 26.2-mile city marathon on the path shown. She expects to need at least 4 hours to finish the race, but hopes to finish in less than 5 hours.
Question: How many miles should Evelyn try to run each hour to reach her goal?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A course map labeled City Marathon 26.2 miles, with numbered mile markers and water stops from start to finish.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Divide the distance by each time to find the pace. In 5 hours: 26.2 ÷ 5 = 5.24 miles per hour. In 4 hours: 26.2 ÷ 4 = 6.55 miles per hour. So Evelyn needs to average between 5.24 and 6.55 miles each hour. Running slower than 5.24 mph puts her over 5 hours, and she does not need to run faster than 6.55 mph.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do you divide with decimals?
conceptIntro.intro: Dividing splits a total into equal groups. When you divide by a decimal, first move the point to make the divisor a whole number — then run the same long-division cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Slide the decimal point the same number of places to the right in BOTH the divisor and the dividend. Write the answer's decimal point in the column directly above the dividend's point. Then repeat Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and long division needs a whole-number divisor.
STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor, so 6.3 becomes 63.
I slide the decimal point 1 place to the right in the dividend too, so 18.9 becomes 189. Both points slid the same 1 place, so the answer does not change. The problem is now 189 ÷ 63.

Now I write it the tall way — 63 into 189 — with the answer going on top of the bar and the answer's decimal point in the column directly above the dividend's point. Then I repeat the same four steps I always use: DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, SUBTRACT, BRING DOWN.
DIVIDE: 63 does not fit into 1 or 18, so my first working number is 189. How many 63s fit into 189? Three. I write 3 above the 9.
BRING DOWN: there are no digits left to bring down, so the cycle is finished and the remainder is 0. 18.9 ÷ 6.3 = 3.
I check by multiplying: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correct — 3 pods can be filled.
linesEs: Quiero 18.9 ÷ 6.3. El divisor es 6.3, y la división larga necesita un divisor entero.
Paso 0 — mueve el punto: muevo el punto decimal 1 lugar a la derecha en el divisor, así que 6.3 se convierte en 63.

Deslizo el punto decimal 1 lugar a la derecha en el dividendo también, así que 18.9 se convierte en 189. Los dos puntos se deslizaron el mismo lugar, así que la respuesta no cambia. El problema ahora es 189 ÷ 63.

Ahora lo escribo en vertical — 189 entre 63 — con la respuesta arriba de la línea y el punto decimal de la respuesta en la columna justo arriba del punto del dividendo. Luego repito los mismos cuatro pasos de siempre: divide, multiplica, resta, baja.
Divide: el 63 no cabe en 1 ni en 18, así que mi primer número de trabajo es 189. ¿Cuántos 63 caben en 189? Tres. Escribo 3 arriba del 9.
Baja: no quedan dígitos por bajar, así que el ciclo termina y el residuo es 0. 18.9 ÷ 6.3 = 3.
Lo compruebo multiplicando: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correcto — se pueden llenar 3 cápsulas.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's do 8.4 ÷ 2.1. STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: how many places make 2.1 a whole number? (1 place, so 2.1 becomes 21.)
Now slide the decimal point 1 place to the right in the dividend too. What does 8.4 become? (84, so the new problem is 84 ÷ 21.)
DIVIDE: 84 ÷ 21 → 4. MULTIPLY: 4 × 21 = 84. SUBTRACT: 84 − 84 = 0. BRING DOWN: nothing is left, so 8.4 ÷ 2.1 = 4. Check: 2.1 × 4 = 8.4.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: Hagamos 8.4 ÷ 2.1. Paso 0 — mueve el punto: ¿cuántos lugares hacen que 2.1 sea un número entero? (1 lugar, así que 2.1 se convierte en 21.)
Ahora desliza el punto decimal 1 lugar a la derecha en el dividendo también. ¿En qué se convierte 8.4? (En 84, así que el nuevo problema es 84 ÷ 21.)
Divide: 84 ÷ 21 → 4. Multiplica: 4 × 21 = 84. Resta: 84 − 84 = 0. Baja: no queda nada, así que 8.4 ÷ 2.1 = 4. Comprueba: 2.1 × 4 = 8.4.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — with support

Remember the key idea: Slide the decimal point the same number of places to the right in BOTH the divisor and the dividend. Write the answer's decimal point in the column directly above the dividend's point. Then repeat Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down..

Recuerda la idea clave: Desliza el punto decimal la misma cantidad de lugares a la derecha en el divisor y en el dividendo. Escribe el punto decimal de la respuesta en la columna justo arriba del punto del dividendo. Luego repite Divide → Multiplica → Resta → Baja.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Construyámoslo juntos — ¿Cómo se divide con decimales?
conceptIntro.introEs: Dividir reparte un total en grupos iguales. Cuando divides entre un decimal, primero mueve el punto para que el divisor sea un número entero — y luego corre el mismo ciclo de división larga: divide, multiplica, resta, baja. Veremos un ejemplo resuelto, haremos uno juntos y luego harás algunos con pistas disponibles cuando las necesites.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Desliza el punto decimal la misma cantidad de lugares a la derecha en el divisor y en el dividendo. Escribe el punto decimal de la respuesta en la columna justo arriba del punto del dividendo. Luego repite Divide → Multiplica → Resta → Baja.

explore.instructionsEs: Calentamiento rápido en grupo: Completa la tabla. Primero desliza el punto decimal a la derecha hasta que el divisor sea un número entero, deslizándolo el mismo número de lugares en los dos números. Luego corre el ciclo de la división larga — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — para hallar el cociente.
columnsEs: Vuelve a escribirlo: desliza los dos puntos

choiceFeedback: The decimal point slid in the wrong direction. Since 1.2 fits into 14.4 more than once, the quotient has to be greater than 1.
Check: 1.2 × 1.2 is only 1.44, not 14.4 — the decimal slid one place too far. Multiply both numbers by 10 so the problem becomes 144 ÷ 12.
That result is 10 times too large — a sign the decimal point moved in only one of the numbers. Scale the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is awkward — notice the divisor 1.2 has one decimal place. There's a move that makes it whole.
Multiply BOTH numbers by 10: scaling dividend and divisor the same way keeps the quotient exactly the same.
Compute 14.4 × 10 = 144 and 1.2 × 10 = 12. Now solve 144 ÷ 12 — a whole-number division you already know how to do.
hintsEs: Dividir entre un decimal es incómodo: fíjate que el divisor 1.2 tiene un lugar decimal. Hay un movimiento que lo vuelve entero.
Multiplica AMBOS números por 10: escalar el dividendo y el divisor igual deja el cociente exactamente igual.
Calcula 14.4 × 10 = 144 y 1.2 × 10 = 12. Ahora resuelve 144 ÷ 12, una división de enteros que ya sabes hacer.

choiceFeedback: The digits are right, but the decimal point moved two places the wrong way. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a quotient larger than the number you started with.
Your digits are right, but the decimal point is one place too far left. Since 0.6 is less than 1, the quotient must be greater than 3.78.
63 × 0.6 = 37.8, ten times too big — the decimal point moved one place too far right. After multiplying both numbers by 10, you divide 37.8 by 6, so the quotient keeps a decimal.
hints: The divisor 0.6 has one decimal place — shifting both numbers one place makes the divisor a whole number.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to build an equivalent problem, then divide, keeping the decimal point in the dividend.
3.78 × 10 = 37.8 and 0.6 × 10 = 6. Now compute 37.8 ÷ 6, keeping the decimal point lined up in your answer.
hintsEs: El divisor 0.6 tiene un lugar decimal: mover ambos números un lugar convierte al divisor en entero.
Multiplica ambos números por 10 para armar un problema equivalente y luego divide, cuidando el punto decimal del dividendo.
3.78 × 10 = 37.8 y 0.6 × 10 = 6. Ahora calcula 37.8 ÷ 6, manteniendo el punto decimal alineado en tu respuesta.

choiceFeedback: The decimal point went the wrong way. 0.7 fits into 8.4 many times, so the quotient is much larger than 1.
Check: 1.2 × 0.7 is only 0.84, not 8.4 — the answer is ten times too small. Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 84 ÷ 7, then divide.
You multiplied 8.4 by 10 but left 0.7 alone. Both numbers have to grow by the same factor for the quotient to stay the same.
hints: Ask yourself: how many groups of 0.7 fit inside 8.4? Since 0.7 is less than 1, expect MORE groups than 8.
Scale both numbers by 10 so you're dividing by a whole number instead of a decimal.
8.4 becomes 84 and 0.7 becomes 7. Solve 84 ÷ 7 — your 7s times-table facts will carry you there.
hintsEs: Pregúntate: ¿cuántos grupos de 0.7 caben en 8.4? Como 0.7 es menor que 1, espera MÁS de 8 grupos.
Escala ambos números por 10 para dividir entre un número entero en lugar de un decimal.
8.4 se vuelve 84 y 0.7 se vuelve 7. Resuelve 84 ÷ 7: la tabla del 7 te lleva directo.

choiceFeedback: Check: 1.2 × 1.3 is only 1.56, not 15.6 — the decimal shifted a place too far. Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 156 ÷ 13, then divide.
13 is the divisor after scaling, not the quotient. You still have to divide 156 by 13.
This result is 10 times too large. Check that you multiplied both 15.6 and 1.3 by the same power of 10 before dividing.
hints: The divisor 1.3 isn't a whole number — shift both numbers before you divide anything.
Multiply dividend and divisor by 10, then divide. Check at the end: your answer times 1.3 should rebuild 15.6.
15.6 × 10 = 156 and 1.3 × 10 = 13. Now count how many 13s fit into 156 — start by trying 13 × 10.
hintsEs: El divisor 1.3 no es entero: mueve ambos números antes de dividir nada.
Multiplica dividendo y divisor por 10 y luego divide. Comprueba al final: tu respuesta por 1.3 debe reconstruir 15.6.
15.6 × 10 = 156 y 1.3 × 10 = 13. Ahora cuenta cuántos 13 caben en 156; empieza probando 13 × 10.

approaching.label: Rewrite each problem by making the divisor a whole number, then solve.
hints: The 'Multiply Both By' column is the key move: choose 10 or 100 based on how many decimal places the DIVISOR has.
One decimal place in the divisor means multiply both numbers by 10; then rewrite and divide whole numbers.
Row 1: 0.9 has one decimal place, so multiply 4.5 and 0.9 each by 10 and write the new whole-number problem in the row.
approaching.explanation: Multiplying the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10 slides both decimal points without changing the quotient. Each divisor here has one decimal place, so ×10 rewrites 4.5 ÷ 0.9 as 45 ÷ 9 = 5 and 3.6 ÷ 0.4 as 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplicar el dividendo y el divisor por la misma potencia de 10 mueve los dos puntos decimales sin cambiar el cociente. Aquí cada divisor tiene un lugar decimal, así que ×10 reescribe 4.5 ÷ 0.9 como 45 ÷ 9 = 5 y 3.6 ÷ 0.4 como 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
approaching.labelEs: Reescribe cada problema convirtiendo el divisor en un número entero y después resuelve.
hintsEs: La columna 'Multiplicar Ambos Por' es el movimiento clave: elige 10 o 100 según cuántos decimales tenga el DIVISOR.
Un decimal en el divisor significa multiplicar ambos números por 10; luego reescribe y divide números enteros.
Fila 1: 0.9 tiene un lugar decimal, así que multiplica 4.5 y 0.9 por 10 y escribe el nuevo problema de enteros en la fila.

approaching.label: Solve each decimal division problem.
hints: Every row uses the same move: shift both numbers until the divisor is whole, then divide as usual.
Count the divisor's decimal places to pick ×10 or ×100 — a divisor like 0.24 needs ×100 — then divide the new whole numbers.
Row 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 becomes 96 ÷ 8 after multiplying both by 10. Solve that, then apply the same shift to every other row.
approaching.explanation: Once the divisor is shifted to a whole number, each row is ordinary division: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7, and 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (that row needs ×100 because 0.24 has two decimal places). The last row becomes 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, since only the divisor has to end up whole.
approaching.explanationEs: Una vez que el divisor se convierte en entero, cada fila es una división común: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7 y 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (esa fila necesita ×100 porque 0.24 tiene dos lugares decimales). La última fila queda como 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, ya que solo el divisor tiene que quedar entero.
approaching.labelEs: Resuelve cada problema de división de decimales.
hintsEs: Cada fila usa el mismo movimiento: mueve ambos números hasta que el divisor sea entero y luego divide normalmente.
Cuenta los decimales del divisor para elegir ×10 o ×100 — un divisor como 0.24 necesita ×100 — y luego divide los nuevos enteros.
Fila 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 se vuelve 96 ÷ 8 al multiplicar ambos por 10. Resuélvelo y aplica el mismo cambio en todas las demás filas.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Move the divisor's decimal
workedExample.labelEs: Mueve el punto decimal del divisor
workedExample.workEs: 0.8 se convierte en 8 (movido 1 lugar a la derecha).

onLevel.correctWork: The student moved the decimal point in the divisor (0.8 → 8) but forgot to move it the same 1 place in the dividend. You must move BOTH: 6.4 becomes 64, so 64 ÷ 8 = 8. So 6.4 ÷ 0.8 = 8. Check: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4. ✓
hints: When you moved 0.8 to 8, what did you have to do to 6.4 as well?
Move the decimal the same 1 place in both: 6.4 → 64, then 64 ÷ 8 = 8.
onLevel.explanation: In the last step 6.4 was divided by the new whole-number divisor without being shifted itself. Both numbers have to move the same 1 place, so 6.4 becomes 64 and the problem is 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Checking confirms it: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el último paso se dividió 6.4 entre el nuevo divisor entero sin moverlo también. Los dos números tienen que moverse el mismo 1 lugar, así que 6.4 se convierte en 64 y el problema es 64 ÷ 8 = 8. La comprobación lo confirma: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante movió el punto decimal del divisor (0.8 → 8) pero olvidó moverlo el mismo 1 lugar en el dividendo. Debes mover AMBOS: 6.4 se convierte en 64, así que 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Por lo tanto 6.4 ÷ 0.8 = 8. Comprueba: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4. ✓
hintsEs: Cuando moviste 0.8 a 8, ¿qué tuviste que hacerle también a 6.4?
Mueve el decimal el mismo lugar en ambos: 6.4 → 64, luego 64 ÷ 8 = 8.

onLevel.stem: A water tank holds 19.2 liters. It is poured into bottles that each hold 1.6 liters. How many bottles can be filled?
choiceFeedback: The digits look right—how many total decimal places should the product have?
Check the division: make the divisor a whole number by moving both decimals one place (192 ÷ 16), then divide.
That is one bottle more than the division gives. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 192 by 16 carefully — it comes out even, with nothing left over.
hints: You're asking how many 1.6s fit into 19.2 — that's division, and the divisor 1.6 needs to become whole first.
Multiply both amounts by 10 to build an equivalent whole-number division, then divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 and 1.6 × 10 = 16. Now run the cycle on 192 ÷ 16: DIVIDE 19 ÷ 16 → 1, MULTIPLY 1 × 16 = 16, SUBTRACT 19 − 16 = 3, BRING DOWN the 2.
onLevel.stemEs: Un tanque de agua contiene 19.2 litros. Se vacía en botellas que contienen 1.6 litros cada una. ¿Cuántas botellas se pueden llenar?
hintsEs: Estás preguntando cuántos 1.6 caben en 19.2: eso es división, y el divisor 1.6 debe volverse entero primero.
Multiplica ambas cantidades por 10 para armar una división equivalente de enteros y luego divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 y 1.6 × 10 = 16. Ahora repite el ciclo en 192 ÷ 16: DIVIDE 19 ÷ 16 → 1, MULTIPLICA 1 × 16 = 16, RESTA 19 − 16 = 3, BAJA el 2.

choiceFeedback: Check: 0.8 × 0.6 is only 0.48, so 0.8 is ten times too small. Multiply both numbers by 10 first — then it's just 48 ÷ 6 with no extra decimal shift.
That looks like a subtraction (4.8 − 0.6) rather than a division. Reread the operation sign.
Ten times too large — that happens when only 4.8 gets multiplied by 10. Scale both numbers the same way.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is easiest when the divisor is a whole number. Ask yourself what 0.6 needs to become.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10. Here, multiplying by 10 does the job.
Multiplying both by 10 turns the problem into 48 ÷ 6. Carry out that division to finish.

onLevel.stem: A ribbon is 7.2 meters long and is cut into 0.8-meter pieces. How many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: Careful — the 7 comes from 7.2, not from dividing. Set up 72 ÷ 8 and work it out.
8 pieces would use only 8 × 0.8 = 6.4 meters, leaving ribbon left over. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 72 by 8 to count every piece.
A little too high. Ten pieces of 0.8 meters would need 8 meters of ribbon, and you only have 7.2.
onLevel.stemEs: Un listón mide 7.2 metros de largo y se corta en pedazos de 0.8 metros. ¿Cuántos pedazos hay?
hints: Cutting a length into equal pieces is a division: total length ÷ length of one piece.
Make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both 7.2 and 0.8 by 10.
That turns the problem into 72 ÷ 8. Count how many 8s fit into 72.
hintsEs: Cortar una longitud en pedazos iguales es una división: longitud total ÷ longitud de un pedazo.
Convierte el divisor en número entero multiplicando 7.2 y 0.8 por 10.
Eso convierte el problema en 72 ÷ 8. Cuenta cuántos 8 caben en 72.

onLevel.explanation: Dividing by 0.25 is like multiplying by 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
choiceFeedback: Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result larger, not smaller. 0.6 is far below 15.
That is 15 ÷ 10. Dividing by 0.25 is not the same as sliding the decimal point one place.
Move both decimals two places so the divisor is whole: 1500 ÷ 25 = 60. Dividing by a number smaller than 1 makes the result LARGER, not smaller.
onLevel.explanationEs: Dividir entre 0.25 es lo mismo que multiplicar por 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
hints: Think about how many quarters fit inside one whole — 0.25 is one quarter.
If four 0.25s fit in every 1, then dividing by 0.25 does the same job as multiplying by 4.
So the problem becomes 15 × 4. Work that product out.
hintsEs: Piensa cuántos cuartos caben en un entero: 0.25 es un cuarto.
Si cuatro veces 0.25 caben en cada 1, entonces dividir entre 0.25 hace lo mismo que multiplicar por 4.
Así el problema se convierte en 15 × 4. Calcula ese producto.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Decimals is moving the decimal point in the divisor but forgetting to move it the same number of places in the dividend. For example, in 6.4 ÷ 0.8 a student changes 0.8 to 8 but leaves the dividend as 6.4, then divides 6.4 ÷ 8 = 0.8 instead of moving both points to get 64 ÷ 8 = 8. A second version of this mistake happens when the divisor has two decimal places, like 0.12: students move both points only 1 place instead of 2, turning 9.6 ÷ 0.12 into 96 ÷ 1.2 instead of the correct 960 ÷ 12. Count the divisor's decimal places first, then move BOTH points that same number of places.

connect.scenario: A ribbon is 16.8 feet long. You need to cut it into pieces that are each 2.4 feet long for a craft project.
connect.promptQuestion: How does decimal division help you figure out how many pieces you can cut?

check.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 10 to clear the decimal: 168 ÷ 24 = 7. Check: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.
check.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos números por 10 para quitar el decimal: 168 ÷ 24 = 7. Comprueba: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.

choices: Because decimals are not allowed in division
Because you always drop the decimal point
Multiplying both numbers by 10 keeps the quotient the same
check.explanation: Division compares two amounts. Scaling both by the same factor of 10 does not change how many times one fits into the other.
check.stemEs: ¿Por qué puedes volver a escribir 16.8 ÷ 2.4 como 168 ÷ 24?
check.explanationEs: La división compara dos cantidades. Escalar las dos por el mismo factor de 10 no cambia cuántas veces una cabe en la otra.
choicesEs: Porque no se permiten decimales en la división
Porque siempre se quita el punto decimal
Multiplicar los dos números por 10 mantiene el mismo cociente

check.stem: If each piece were 2.8 feet instead, how many whole pieces could you cut?
check.explanation: 16.8 ÷ 2.8 = 6. Longer pieces means fewer of them fit.
check.stemEs: Si cada pieza fuera de 2.8 pies, ¿cuántas piezas enteras podrías cortar?
check.explanationEs: 16.8 ÷ 2.8 = 6. Piezas más largas significan que caben menos.

connect.modelAnswer: 16.8 ÷ 2.4 = 7 pieces. Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 168 ÷ 24 = 7, then check by multiplying back: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.
connect.scenarioEs: Un listón mide 16.8 pies de largo. Necesitas cortarlo en piezas de 2.4 pies cada una para un proyecto de manualidades.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Cómo te ayuda la división de decimales a averiguar cuántas piezas puedes cortar?
connect.modelAnswerEs: 16.8 ÷ 2.4 = 7 piezas. Multiplica los dos números por 10 para obtener 168 ÷ 24 = 7, y luego comprueba multiplicando de regreso: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.

questions.stem: A baker has 50 rolls. Each box holds 6 rolls. How many boxes are filled, and how many rolls are left over?
questions.explanation: 6 × 8 = 48, and 50 − 48 = 2. So 8 boxes are filled and 2 rolls are left over.
